meta.source: NSDL fortnightly sector-wise FPI investment data (fpi.nsdl.co.in StaticReports; official, published per fortnight)

definitions.auc_cr: Assets Under Custody of FPIs in that sector's equities at the fortnight end — a LEVEL, and it moves with price as well as flow.
definitions.flow_cr: FPI NET INVESTMENT in that sector's equities during the fortnight — a FLOW, as published by NSDL (not inferred from ΔAUC).
definitions.total: NSDL's own published Grand Total row, not a sum of sectors — so it is taxonomy-independent and honestly continuous across the whole history.
definitions.sector: the modern NSE macro-sector taxonomy, 102 fortnights (2022-04-30 onward).
definitions.sector_legacy: the older BSE-classification taxonomy NSDL used until 2024-07, 234 fortnights, under its OWN sector names.
definitions.bridge: legacy sectors summed into their modern equivalent and spliced onto the modern series. Read `quality` and `legacy_components` before quoting it: 'exact' means the perimeters match, 'approx' means a real boundary moved, 'modern_only' means there is no honest pre-2024 counterpart (null).

meta.excluded: rows named ('sovereign', 'others', 'total', 'grand total') are not equity sectors (Sovereign is government debt) and are excluded from the sector sets; child rows (Sr. No. '2a'/'2b') are excluded from every aggregate because their parent already contains them
caveats: Fortnightly, published a few days after each period end.
AUC is custody VALUE (price + flow); never infer flow from ΔAUC — use flow_cr.

The sector TAXONOMY changed at 2024-08. `sector` and `sector_legacy` are different classifications and must not be concatenated; use `bridge` (and read its quality flag) or `total` for a continuous series.
Debt/Hybrid/MF/AIF asset classes exist in the source but are excluded here; summing them with equity is meaningless.
USD columns embed the period's exchange rate — prefer INR for time series.
